sections.text: Third parties, including contractors, consultants, and vendors, may receive access to company systems only when sponsored by a named employee who is responsible for their activity. Before access is granted, the third party must sign a non-disclosure agreement and the vendor must complete a security assessment. Vendors that will process Restricted data must also provide an independent security certification report and receive approval from the CISO.

Third-party accounts are individual and named, and shared accounts are prohibited. All third-party access requires multi-factor authentication under SEC-302. Access is limited to the systems and data needed for the contracted work and is granted for a maximum of 90 days, after which the sponsor must request renewal. Remote access to production systems is permitted only through the company bastion host, and all such sessions are recorded.

Sponsors review the access of their third parties every quarter and confirm that it is still required. Access must be removed within 24 hours of a contract ending or when the third party no longer needs it. Accounts with no login activity for 30 days are disabled automatically. The Security team may suspend third-party access immediately when there is a suspected security incident.
